Elena (Support): Customer on private VPC installer fails when fetching model shards and calling KMS; logs show TLS errors + 403 KMS. They need an allowlist + quick repro steps.

Customer Ops: Pasted truncated log: 
``
GET https://models-cdn.redwood-inference.com/shard-7 -> timeout
curl: (35) SSL_connect error
POST https://kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ -> 403

Traceback: requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 403
```

Ryan (Onprem Eng): Short checklist: allow outbound TCP 443 for FQDNs below, preserve SNI/ALPN, avoid TLS MITM for these hosts or install proxy CA in node truststore. Also check system clock and MTU if large shard transfers reset.

Ryan (Onprem Eng): Minimal FQDN allowlist (replace region/account when needed):
- models-cdn.redwood-inference.com:443
- model-registry.redwood-inference.com:443
- packages.redwood-inference.com:443
- files.pythonhosted.org:443
- pypi.org:443
- auth.redwood-inference.com:443
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com:443 (optional)
- kms.<region>.amazonaws.com:443 or cloudkms.googleapis.com:443
- ocsp.digicert.com:443 (if TLS intercept)

Vikram (SRE): 403 from KMS often means IAM/signature failure, but if the egress proxy rewrites Host or strips headers, SigV4 fails. Also check source IP allowlists on customer-managed KMS. Run `date -u` to rule out clock skew.

Caroline (Security): Diagnostic commands to run from failing node (paste outputs):
``
# DNS
dig +short models-cdn.redwood-inference.com
# TLS handshake + ALPN
openssl s_client -connect models-cdn.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername models-cdn.redwood-inference.com -alpn h2,http/1.1 -showcerts
# curl verbose
curl -v --max-time 30 https://models-cdn.redwood-inference.com/shard-7 || true
# test KMS endpoint (region adjust)
curl -v -X POST https://kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ -H 'Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.1' -d '{}' || true
# MTU / resets (run near transfer)
ping -M do -s 1400 models-cdn.redwood-inference.com || true
# check tcp resets
sudo journalctl -u networking -n 200 | tail -n 50 || true
# system clock
date -u
```

Elena (Support): Note: if corporate firewall enforces per-destination ACLs, KMS 403 can surface when KMS requests originate from NAT IPs that KMS denies (customer-managed allowlists). Confirm with security team that NAT IPs are allowed in KMS console or that role-based access is used.

Vikram (SRE): If `openssl s_client` shows a cert issued by the corporate proxy, either bypass proxy for these hosts or import the proxy CA into /etc/ssl/certs. For large file timeouts, check proxy idle timeouts and chunk buffering.

Caroline (Security): If they must IP allowlist, we can provide a current CDN prefix snapshot privately, but prefixes rotate. Strongly prefer FQDN allowlist. If the proxy does TLS inspection and they can't change it, ensure OCSP responder hosts (ocsp.*) are reachable.

Customer Ops: Running these now, will paste outputs. Quick question: we see intermittent TCP RSTs during shard download. Could that be MTU or a firewall dropping large segments?

Ryan (Onprem Eng): Yes—path MTU, transparent proxy MSS clamping, or a stateful firewall with connection size limits can cause RSTs. Ask infra to temporarily bypass for a test host. Also check any inline DLP appliance.

Elena (Support): I'll open ticket SUP-5621 and request the dig/openssl/curl outputs + date -u. @Ryan can you DM the CDN prefix CSV if they insist on IPs?

Ryan (Onprem Eng): Will DM prefix CSV and region mapping. :thumbsup:
